Review pyproject.toml lines 39-46 (core deps) and 59-116 (optional extras).
The minimal change: remove line 40 from [project.dependencies] and add a new stanza
to [project.optional-dependencies]:
  duckdb = ["duckdb>=1.0.0"]
Then add "duckdb" (or the extras spec) to the `dev`, `all`, and `local` groups.
Regenerate uv.lock with `uv lock` and verify the pin is gone from the core set.
description:
DuckDB is currently a core (required) dependency in pyproject.toml at line 40:
  "duckdb>=1.4.0"

Because it's required, uv.lock pins it to an exact version (currently 1.4.3). When a
user runs `uv run benchbox run`, uv syncs the environment against uv.lock BEFORE Python
starts, silently reverting any manually installed version (e.g., duckdb==1.5.0.dev307)
back to 1.4.3. The user has no visibility into this until they check the result JSON.

Moving duckdb to an optional extras group removes it from the lock-enforced core set.
uv would no longer revert it - whatever the user has installed survives. Users who want
DuckDB can install it via `pip install benchbox[duckdb]` or the existing `all` extra.

Design decisions to resolve during implementation:
  1. Minimum version for the optional duckdb extra - keep >=1.4.0 or relax to >=1.0.0?
     Relaxing to >=1.0.0 gives users maximum flexibility (they can test any version),
     though some BenchBox features may require newer APIs.
  2. Backward compatibility - `pip install benchbox` currently installs duckdb; removing
     it from core will break existing installs. Options:
       a. Add duckdb to a "local" or "embedded" extras group and update install docs.
       b. Add duckdb to the existing `all` meta-extra and mark it as the recommended install.
       c. Keep a minimal >=1.0.0 pin in core (so something is installed) but remove the
          tight lock on a specific version by using a pre-release-tolerant spec.
  3. The `dev` extras group at line 66 also includes "duckdb>=1.4.0" - must be updated
     to match whatever approach is chosen.
  4. CI must still work - the CI install likely uses `pip install -e .[dev]` or similar.

The primary goal is: after `pip install benchbox` (or `uv add benchbox`), a user who
then runs `uv pip install "duckdb==X.Y.Z"` should have that version respected by
`uv run benchbox run` without being silently reverted.

anti_patterns.dont: remove duckdb from the 'dev' extras group without replacing it
anti_patterns.instead: update dev group at the same time as core

anti_patterns.dont: set an upper bound on the optional duckdb extra (e.g., duckdb>=1.0.0,<2.0)
anti_patterns.why: that defeats the purpose of allowing dev/future versions

anti_patterns.instead: update README and getting-started in the same PR
anti_patterns.why: users will get ImportError with no explanation
